Indian Standard 



DETERMINATION OF INSOLUBLE (FREE) CARBON IN 
HARDMETALS BY GRAVIMETRIC METHODS 



1. Scope 

1.1 This standard specifies a gravimetric method for the determination of the insoluble ( free) carbon 
content in carbides and hardmetals. 

1.2 This method is applicable to the following, having carbon content between 002 and 0'5 percent 
(m/m): 

a) Carbides of hafnium, molybdenum, niobium, tantalum, titanium, vanadium, tungsten and 
zirconium; 

b) Mixtures of these carbides and binder metals, free of lubricant; and 

c) All grades of presintered or sintered hardmetals produced from these carbides. 

2. Principle — Decomposition of the carbides and determination of the insoluble carbon by a 
gravimetric method. 

3. Reagents — During the analysis, use only reagents of analytical grade and distilled water or water 
of equivalent purity. 

3.1 Dilute Nitric Acid ( p = V20 g/ml ) — Add 2 000 ml of concentrated nitric acid ( p — 1 42 g/ml ) to 
3 000 ml of water. 

3.2 Hydrofluoric Acid ( 9 = V12 gjml ) 

4. Apparatus 

4.0 Ordinary Laboratory Apparatus 

4.1 Apparatus — Specified in IS : 12539-1988 Determination of total carbon in hardmetal by gravimetric 
method'. 

4.2 Platinum Dish of Capacity 200 ml 

4.3 Filter Device — Ceramic filter device or bed of suitable refractory fibrous or powder material in a 
Gooch crucible. 

Note — if necessary, pretreat the refractory material at BOO to 1 000°C under strongly oxidizing condition for a 
minimum of 3 h. Store it in a desiccator, if pretreated. 

4.4 Vacuum Filteration Assembly 

5. Sampling 

5.1 The sample shall be crushed to a powder in mortar made of a material which does not alter the 
sample composition. The powder shall pass through a 180 Mm sieve. 

Note — For sintered hardmetals, the preparation of sample shall bo as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the manufacturer. 

5.2 The analysis shall be carried out on two or three test portions. 

6. Procedure 

6.1 Test Portion — Weigh to the nearest 01 g, approximately 25 g of the test sample. 

6.2 Dissolution —Transfer the test portion into a platinum dish. Add 75 ml of dilute nitric acid ( 3.1 ) 
and place the dish on a steam bath for 5 min. Add, drop by drop, 10 ml of hydrofluoric acid ( 3*2 ), and 
leave the dish on steam bath for about 1 h until complete dissolution is obtained. Cool the solution to 
ambient temperature.

CAU TION — Hydrofluoric and nitric acids are very dangerous chemicals- Any contact with 
these acids or inhalation of their vapours must be avoided. All operations with these acids shall 
be carried out in a fume-cupboard with good ventilation. 

6.3 Preparation of Gooch Crucible — Insert the ceramic filter (4.3) into the crucible. If a refractory 
material is used, fill the crusible to a depth of approximately 8 to 10 mm and press it down so that the 
residue will be retained on the refractory material and at the same time filtering will not be too slow. 

6.4 Filtering — Before filtering, add a limited quantity of water to avoid the precipitation of tungstic 
acid. Filter the contents of the dish (see 6.2) through the filter device (4.3). Rinse the dish twice 
with small volume of water. Be sure that all particles of carbon are transferred to the filtering 
device. Rinse the dish again with water at least twice and thereafter wash the filter device free from 
acid with hot water ( about 500 ml is usually needed ). 

Remove the wet filter device from the Gooch crucibie and transfer the wet filter device into a 
boat. Dry it at 110°C. 

6.5 Blank Test — Carry out two blank tests with each series of determinations. Prepare the Gooch 
crucible according to 6.3. Filter through the filter device (4.3) a mixture of 75 ml dilute nitric 
acid (3.1 ) and 10 ml hydrofluoric acid ( 3.2), and proceed according to 6.4. 

6.6 Determination — Burn the filter device (4.3) in a stream of oxygen in accordance with IS : 12539- 
1988. Use a furnace with an inner temperature of tube of approximately 1 200°C. 

7. Test Results 

7.1 Calculation — The carbon content, expressed as a percentage by mass, is given by the formula: 



Insoluble ( free ) carbon, ( percent by mass ) = 27*29 x 



m 2 — m-i 



m 

where 

m = mass in g, of the test portion; 

mi = mass in g, of carbon dioxide obtained from the blank test; 

m* = mass in g, of carbon dioxide obtained from the combustion of the test portion; 
and 

27'29 — carbon dioxide to carbon conversion factor, multiplied by 100. 

7.2 Tolerance — The deviations between two or three independent determinations shall not exceed the 
values shown in Table 1. 

TABLE 1 TOLERANCE

Percent Percent Percent 

From 002 up to 010 002 003 

Over 0'10 up to 50 004 0*05 

7.3 Final Result — Report the arithmetical mean of acceptable determinations rounded to the nearest 
0*01 percent. 

8. Test Report — The test report shaii include the foiiowing information: 

a) Reference to this standard, 

b) All details necessary for identification of the test sample, 

c) The result obtained, and 

d) Details of any occurrence which may have affected the result. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 3508-1985 'Hardmetais 
— Determination of insoluble free carbon content — Gravimetric method' issued by the International 
Organization for Standardization ( ISO ).
